bullets.title: META Muse: Consensus bull case solidifies; +11% day, SHOP/PYPL partner, AMZN blocks
bullets.body: META closed up +11% (best day since Apr '25) on Muse momentum — 1.8M iOS downloads vs 1.3M ChatGPT at equivalent launch stage, 2.5M total since debut. SHOP +7% after CEO announces agentic checkout partnership; PYPL +4% on similar deal announced 9/22. AMZN blocked Muse from its marketplace citing privacy/security, which analysts read as validation of the threat to its $68B ads business. JPM reiterates OW with $820 PT; Hedgeye flipped META to bullish TREND signal.

bullets.title: META Muse agentic commerce disruption basket down 12%; EXPE/BKNG/DASH in crosshairs
bullets.body: The agentic commerce disruption short basket is down 12% since Muse's 9/8 launch vs META +20%. MS podcast (Brian Nowak) frames BKNG/ABNB as better positioned vs EXPE given unique inventory; DASH and CART weighed down by GOOGL UCP positive sentiment. Subscription inertia reduction (8%→4% monthly renewals) seen as structural threat to OTAs, food delivery, and lead-gen platforms. Analyst analogy to GLP-1 disruption basket: early shorts eventually down 50-70%.

bullets.title: PSKY-WBD merger clears regulatory hurdle; closes in ~2 weeks, $6B synergies preserved
bullets.body: PSKY settled antitrust case with California and other states, clearing path for the $110B WBD merger expected to close within ~2 weeks before ticking fees (starting Oct 1) become a burden. Settlement terms include 30-32 films/year output commitment, $1.5B U.S. production spend over 5 years, CNN/CBS editorial independence board, and independent monitor. MS raises PSKY PT to $11.50 (from $10.00), sees path to >240M subscribers post-merger. WBD +11% on merger clarity; PSKY +4.3% pre-market.

bullets.title: MSFT: Oppenheimer raises PT to $570; Azure nearing 50% growth, Copilot shifting to usage-based
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raises MSFT PT to $570 post-management meeting. Azure demand exceeds supply; management sees potential for ~50% growth in coming quarters as new capacity comes online. Microsoft plans to double its data-center fleet over two years. Copilot monetization broadening from per-seat ($30/user) to agent-driven token/credit consumption. Key proof points remain usage attach rates, not seat counts.

bullets.title: NFLX: HSBC downgrades to Hold, cuts PT to $76 from $96
bullets.body: HSBC cuts Netflix to Hold from Buy, reducing price target to $76 from $96, implying only ~4% upside. FactSet consensus target is $93.57. No specific fundamental catalyst cited in the downgrade note.

bullets.title: FOXA: UBS maintains Buy, raises Tubi estimate to 25% growth; F27 EBITDA $4.1B intact
bullets.body: UBS raises F1Q Tubi growth estimate to 25% y/y (from 17%) on continued viewership uplift; F1Q EBITDA revised to $1.37B, up ~30% y/y. Total company ad growth expected at 35% y/y in F1Q. F27 EBITDA guidance unchanged at $4.1B supported by World Cup, mid-terms, and cable renewals. Pending ROKU deal seen as long-term net positive for CTV exposure. Stock trades at ~5.5x '28E standalone EBITDA.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS upgrades to Buy, $275 PT on expanded AWS collaboration and Accenture Edge launch
bullets.body: UBS upgrades Accenture to Buy with $275 PT (vs. prior Neutral), citing Accenture Edge — a midmarket platform targeting $300M-$3B revenue companies with six live AWS Marketplace offerings (data discovery, VM migration, contact center, FinOps, AI assurance, cloud security). FY26 inorganic contribution raised to $9B from $5B; cybersecurity now $10B revenue with OT TAM expanded 3x. Q4 earnings due 10/1; NYC Investor Day 10/14.

bullets.title: AVGO: UBS hosts NDR Oct 1 with CEO Hock Tan; Buy/$470 PT reiterated
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Broadcom with $470 PT (~$1.7T market cap) and is hosting a virtual NDR group meeting Oct 1 (12:30-1:25pm ET) with CEO Hock Tan and CFO Amie Thuener. No new rating action; event focused on data center networking, connectivity, and display markets.

bullets.title: INTC/TSM: Intel 18A wins HBM5 base die slot (late 2028); TSMC advanced nodes fully booked
bullets.body: Multiple sources note TSMC advanced nodes are fully booked, positioning Intel 18A as the pragmatic base die partner for HBM5 starting late 2028, with TSMC handling HBM4/HBM4E. Separately, the US Government's 433M INTC share purchase at $20.47 (Aug 2025) is now worth $52.2B at $120.47, an unrealized gain of $43.3B.

bullets.title: AMD: 52-week high (+293% y/y); joins $1T club on CPU/agent demand; GDDR7 Linux groundwork laid
bullets.body: AMD hit a new 52-week high at $618.20 (+292.8% y/y) and joined the $1T market cap club, with ARM +17.1% and INTC +12.1% also rallying on CPU/agentic compute demand. Separately, AMD quietly added GDDR7 support to the Linux kernel, signaling RDNA 5 architecture will upgrade from GDDR6 memory.

bullets.title: NVDA: $1.5B additional investment in SB Energy ahead of IPO; FSD competition rising
bullets.body: NVIDIA increased its cumulative investment in SoftBank-backed SB Energy to $3B ahead of the planned IPO, signaling continued commitment to AI data center infrastructure. SoftBank attracted >$20B preliminary demand for its ~$11B junk bond offering. Separately, a comment at the All-In Summit noted the FSD/autonomous vehicle market will become increasingly crowded.

bullets.title: MDB: Bullish into investor day; AI-native traction, MCP integration, long-term target lift expected
bullets.body: Citi TMT notes MDB is expected to announce AI-native traction and MCP integration with frontier labs at its upcoming investor day, with management likely to lift long-term targets. MDB CEO cited GA of MCP products driving a spike in Atlas traffic. No rating or PT change noted in the summary.

bullets.title: GOOGL/SO nuclear deal: 96MW uprate adds ~$900M customer benefits; TX data center permits halted
bullets.body: Google agreed to fund capacity increases at two Georgia nuclear plants adding ~96MW, enabling ~$900M in customer benefits via a new NU-1 tariff with Southern Company. Texas Governor Abbott separately froze all state-issued data center permits pending an ERCOT grid/water audit — analysts view practical impact as limited but it adds regulatory overhang. LA County also halted new data center developments.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro lead times weak in China (11 days vs. 30 days prior year); hits 52-week high
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max lead times at only 11 days in Mainland China vs. 30 days last year, suggesting softer Chinese demand for the new cycle. US carrier promotions are $100 more aggressive, absorbing the $100 MSRP increase. Despite this, AAPL hit a 52-week high at $340.50 (+38.7% y/y) and is on Hedgeye's bullish TREND signal list alongside MSFT and META.

bullets.title: TSLA: Autonomy 'increasingly real' post site visit; Cybercab cost advantages durable but stock in 'no man's land'
bullets.body: Opco industrials analyst describes TSLA autonomy as "increasingly real" and poised to shift the story in coming quarters, with Cybercab manufacturing showing meaningful innovation and durable cost advantages. However, the stock is characterized as in 'no man's land' with Optimus and robotaxi service still years from commercialization. Investors expected to get excited about autonomous fleet ramps with more modestly valued plays.

bullets.title: EFX: JPM maintains OW; AI cost savings target doubled to $150M, EBITDA margins running above guidance
bullets.body: JPM highlights EFX takeaways from its London All Stars Conference: EWS/Government delivered ~$100M new ACV and ~$200M renewal ACV in 2Q26. AI cost savings target raised to $150M (from $75M) through 2028 with ~40% of headcount in tech. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded +80bps in 1Q26 and +120bps in 2Q26, running above the medium-term +50bps annual outlook. FHFA/VantageScore competitive pressure seen as focused on pricing, not tri-merge elimination.

bullets.title: EVER: Down 13.2% on unusual volume amid agentic AI disintermediation concerns in insurance
bullets.body: StreetAccount flags EVER down 13.2% on 196% of average volume with no company-specific news, linked to broader sector concern that agentic AI agents (like Meta Muse) will disintermediate insurance lead-generation and advisory platforms. AXTA also flagged on unusual volume (122% avg, +3.5%) though with no specific catalyst cited. Multiple insurance/fintech names (GSHD, QNST, ALL, LPLA) also declining on unusual volume.

bullets.title: Banks: JPM sales desk fades weakness; favors MS, PNC, FITB; AI disruption thesis rejected
bullets.body: JPM sales desk attributes aggressive bank selling to positioning unwind (L/S ratio at 82nd percentile), not fundamental repricing from AI disruption. The Muse/agentic AI thesis is explicitly rejected — trust-based banking model is not disintermediable by untrusted consumer AI products. Large cap banks (C, MS, GS, USB) dominating volume while regionals and LAZ, JEF outperform. Favored longs: MS, PNC, FITB.

bullets.title: SHOP: +7% on META Muse partnership; +5.8% pre-market follow-through; +8.1% on TSX
bullets.body: Shopify CEO announced an agentic checkout partnership with Meta Muse on 9/21, driving SHOP +7% that day and +5.8% pre-market on 9/22 (+8.1% on Toronto Stock Exchange). The deal mitigates the agentic commerce bear case for SHOP and positions it as a beneficiary rather than a disruptee. Meta's Muse is currently the #1 App Store ranking since its 9/8 launch.

bullets.title: TSM: Taiwan export orders hit record $104B in Aug (+71% y/y); double-ordering risk flagged
bullets.body: Taiwan export orders surged to $104B in August, +71.4% y/y vs 63% consensus, with US orders alone reaching a record $42B (+88.9% y/y). TSM's TAIEX hit all-time highs and is outperforming. However, PSC Macro flags that actual export growth y/y is slowing, signaling potential double-ordering risk similar to patterns seen in the 1990s.
